nd476f5e723d.s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1892, nominations to the councils were made on the recommendation of bodies such as:
nd476f5e723d.x: The 1892 Act's indirect system worked through recommendations from universities, municipalities and chambers of commerce.

nac3228e7d4c.s: Who was the first Governor-General of India?
nac3228e7d4c.x: William Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833; Canning was the first Viceroy and Hastings the first Governor-General of Bengal.

nindian-polity-22-18.s: Which Act banned private trade and the acceptance of bribes by Company officials?
nindian-polity-22-18.x: The Regulating Act, 1773 banned both private trade and bribes by Company officials.

nindian-polity-22-19.s: Besides overriding his Council, the Act of 1786 empowered the Governor-General to:
nindian-polity-22-19.x: The Act of 1786 gave the Governor-General two separate powers: to override his Council and to act as Commander-in-Chief.

nindian-polity-22-51.s: The High Courts of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were set up in 1862 under the:
nindian-polity-22-51.x: The Indian High Courts Act was passed in 1861 and the three High Courts were set up under it in 1862.

nindian-polity-43-16.s: Which Act restored the legislative powers of Bombay and Madras?
nindian-polity-43-16.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1861 restored the legislative powers of Bombay and Madras; separate electorates came only in 1909.

nindian-polity-1-23.s: Who became the first Indian Law Member of the Viceroy's Executive Council after the 1909 Act?
nindian-polity-1-23.x: The 1909 Act first brought Indians into the Viceroy's and Governors' Executive Councils, and S.P. Sinha became the first Indian Law Member.

nindian-polity-1-25.s: The term 'responsible government' was used for the first time in the:
nindian-polity-1-25.x: The 1919 Act first used the term 'responsible government'; it also made the Central Legislature bicameral and introduced provincial dyarchy.

nindian-polity-1-41.s: Who was the first Chancellor of the Chamber of Princes?
nindian-polity-1-41.x: Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner was the first Chancellor of the 120-member Chamber of Princes created under the 1919 Act.

nindian-polity-38-22.s: Under provincial dyarchy (1919), the transferred subjects were administered by the Governor with the:
nindian-polity-38-22.x: Transferred subjects were under the Governor and popular Ministers; reserved subjects were under the Governor and Executive Council.

n28fe9c75572.s: How many sections did the Government of India Act, 1935 contain?
n28fe9c75572.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 had 321 sections, 14 parts and 10 schedules.

n350222ac172.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, Sindh was separated from:
n350222ac172.x: The 1935 Act separated Burma from India, Sindh from Bombay and Orissa from Bihar.

n8deab8e3fc1.s: Article 175 of the Constitution (Governor's address) corresponds to which Section of the Government of India Act, 1935?
n8deab8e3fc1.x: Section 63 of the 1935 Act dealt with the Governor's address, now Article 175; Section 42 is the ordinance model for Article 123.

nindian-polity-22-33.s: Which Section of the Government of India Act, 1935 is the model for the President's ordinance power under Article 123?
nindian-polity-22-33.x: Section 42 of the 1935 Act is the model for Article 123; the Act's All-India Federation and Central Dyarchy were never implemented.

n71bf00fea44.s: About how many princely states became theoretically free when paramountcy lapsed in 1947?
n71bf00fea44.x: About 565 princely states were theoretically free after paramountcy lapsed, though they were expected to join India or Pakistan.

nindian-polity-22-34.s: Which Act ended British sovereignty over India and gave the Constituent Assembly legislative powers as well?
nindian-polity-22-34.x: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 ended British sovereignty and gave the Constituent Assemblies both constitution-making and legislative powers.

nindian-polity-5-12.s: The restricted franchise used in electing the Constituent Assembly came from the:
nindian-polity-5-12.x: The election used the restricted franchise of the 1935 Act, based on tax, education and property qualifications.

nindian-polity-5-2.s: The elections to the Constituent Assembly were held in:
nindian-polity-5-2.x: The elections were held in July–August 1946, not June–July; the provincial assembly elections had been held in January 1946.

nindian-polity-5-9.s: The principle of a Constituent Assembly was accepted by the British in 1940 through the:
nindian-polity-5-9.x: The August Offer of 1940 accepted the principle; Nehru's clear statement of support had come in 1938.

nindian-polity-5-10.s: The proposal for an elected Constituent Assembly was made in 1942 by the:
nindian-polity-5-10.x: The Cripps Mission of 1942 proposed an elected Constituent Assembly; the Assembly was actually constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.

nindian-polity-5-8.s: The first draft of the Constitution prepared by B.N. Rau contained:
nindian-polity-5-8.x: B.N. Rau, the Constitutional Advisor, prepared the first draft of 243 Articles and 13 Schedules.

nindian-polity-1-31.s: Who was the first permanent Vice-President of the Constituent Assembly?
nindian-polity-1-31.x: H.C. Mukherjee was the first permanent Vice-President; Sinha was the temporary President and Prasad the permanent President from 11 December 1946.

nindian-polity-5-11.s: How many seats did the Muslim League win in the 1946 Constituent Assembly election?
nindian-polity-5-11.x: The Congress won 208 seats, the Muslim League 73 and others 15.

nindian-polity-52-28.s: Which of the following committee – chairman pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribals – Sardar Patel
nindian-polity-52-28.x: The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee was chaired by J.B. Kripalani, not H.C. Mukherjee; Patel chaired the Advisory and Provincial Constitution Committees.

nc1c4b93061e.s: The Draft Constitution was published on:
nc1c4b93061e.x: The Draft Constitution was published on 21 February 1948; 22 January 1947 was the adoption of the Objectives Resolution.

nc27e4ebc6c8.s: How many Articles did the Constitution of India contain as adopted?
nc27e4ebc6c8.x: The Draft had 315 Articles; the Constitution as adopted had 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.

n1d5aa8cefd0.s: Who called the Constituent Assembly 'a body of Hindus'?
n1d5aa8cefd0.x: Viscount Simon called it 'a body of Hindus'; Granville Austin called it a one-party body in an essentially one-party country.

n38ddd350ed1.s: The vesting of residuary powers in the Centre was borrowed from the Constitution of:
n38ddd350ed1.x: Residuary powers with the Centre came from Canada; Australia gave the joint sitting and freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse.

n0834d21b049.s: The ideals of social, economic and political justice in the Preamble were borrowed from:
n0834d21b049.x: These ideals came from the USSR, not Australia; Australia gave the Concurrent List and freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse.

n1d7738bdeec.s: The method of election of the President of India was borrowed from:
n1d7738bdeec.x: The President's election method and nomination to the Rajya Sabha came from Ireland; South Africa gave the amendment procedure and Rajya Sabha elections.

naf93064b6a9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the borrowed parts of the Indian Constitution?
o: The parliamentary system forms part of the political part.
The structure is largely drawn from the Government of India Act, 1935.
Directive Principles form part of the political part.
Fundamental Rights form part of the philosophical part.
naf93064b6a9.x: Directive Principles, like Fundamental Rights, belong to the philosophical part; the parliamentary system is the political part.

nindian-polity-3-3.s: Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from:
nindian-polity-3-3.x: Fundamental Duties came from the USSR, which was also the source of the Preamble's ideals of social, economic and political justice.

n6b7af0236f5.s: In India, residuary powers lie with Parliament under Article:
n6b7af0236f5.x: Article 248 vests residuary powers in Parliament, following Canada; in the USA and Australia they lie with the States.

nfc6f2b5cdee.s: How many subjects does the Union List of the Seventh Schedule now contain?
nfc6f2b5cdee.x: The Union, State and Concurrent Lists now contain 98, 59 and 52 subjects respectively.

new.s: Who was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774)?
new.x: Sir Elijah Impey was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court set up in 1774; Gwyer was the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court (1937).

new.s: The Regulating Act, 1773 followed the report of a committee headed by:
new.x: The Lord North committee report led to the Regulating Act, 1773.

new.s: The Amending Act of 1781, which separated judicial and executive functions, is also known as the:
new.x: The Amending Act 1781 is the Act of Settlement; the Saint Helena Act is the Charter Act of 1833.

new.s: The Court of Directors of the East India Company was abolished in:
new.x: The Court of Directors lasted till 1858, when the Government of India Act abolished it; the Regulating Act did not abolish it.

new.s: The Board of Control was set up by the:
new.x: Pitt's India Act, 1784 set up the Board of Control for political affairs, beside the Court of Directors for commercial affairs.

new.s: How many members did the Board of Control under Pitt's India Act have?
new.x: The Board of Control had 6 members, including a Secretary of State and the Chancellor of the Exchequer.

new.s: Pitt's India Act, 1784 reduced the Governor-General's council to:
new.x: Pitt's India Act cut the council to 3, from the 4 members given by the Regulating Act.

new.s: The Charter Act of 1793 extended the Company's trade monopoly by:
new.x: The Charter Act of 1793 extended the monopoly by 20 years.

new.s: Which Charter Act allowed Christian missionaries to come to India?
new.x: The Charter Act of 1813 allowed Christian missionaries, after efforts by Charles Grant and Wilberforce.

new.s: The legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's council were separated by the:
new.x: The Charter Act of 1853 separated the council's legislative and executive functions and added 6 legislative members.

new.s: Open competition for the civil services, put into operation by the 1853 Act, was worked out by the:
new.x: The 1853 Act put open competition into operation, and the Macaulay Committee of 1854 worked it out.

new.s: Which Section of the Charter Act, 1833 said no Indian would be debarred from office by religion, birth, descent or colour?
new.x: Section 87 of the 1833 Act laid this down, though open competition was only attempted then.

new.s: Who was the first Law Member of the Governor-General's Council?
new.x: Macaulay became the first Law Member under the 1833 Act, not Impey; S.P. Sinha was the first Indian Law Member (1909).

new.s: The Council of India, created in 1858 to assist the Secretary of State, had:
new.x: The 1858 Act created the Secretary of State for India with a 15-member Council of India.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1858:
1. It abolished the Board of Control and the Court of Directors.
2. It created the office of Secretary of State for India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: the 1858 Act abolished the Board of Control and Court of Directors and created the Secretary of State for India.

new.s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1892, the legislative councils could:
o: Discuss the budget but not vote on it
Not discuss the budget at all
new.x: The 1892 Act allowed discussion of the budget without a vote; supplementary questions came only in 1909.

new.s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1892, questions in the councils required a notice of:
new.x: Questions needed 6 days' notice, and no supplementary questions were allowed.

new.s: The portfolio system, begun by Canning in 1859, received statutory recognition in:
new.x: Canning began the portfolio system in 1859; the Indian Councils Act, 1861 gave it statutory recognition.

new.s: Supplementary questions in the legislative councils were first allowed by the:
new.x: The 1892 Act allowed no supplementary questions; the 1909 Act allowed them.

new.s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1909, the total strength of the Central Legislative Council was:
new.x: Additional members rose to 60, making a total of 69 (37 officials and 32 non-officials).

new.s: The Government of India Act, 1919 extended communal representation to:
o: Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans
new.x: The 1919 Act extended it to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans; the 1935 Act added depressed classes, women and labour.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. It provided for direct elections.
2. Its franchise was based on adult suffrage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The 1919 Act brought direct elections, but on a limited franchise of property, tax and education, not adult suffrage.

new.s: The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for a statutory commission after how many years?
new.x: The Act provided for a commission after 10 years; the Simon Commission came in 1927, two years early.

new.s: The Public Service Commission provided by the 1919 Act was set up on:
new.x: The PSC was set up on 1 October 1926; 1 October 1937 was the Federal Court and 1 April 1935 the RBI.

new.s: The Simon Commission, boycotted with 'Simon Go Back', consisted of how many members?
new.x: The Simon Commission had 7 members, all British, chaired by Sir John Simon.

new.s: The Federal Court set up under the 1935 Act was replaced by the Supreme Court in:
new.x: The Federal Court, inaugurated in 1937, was replaced by the Supreme Court in 1950.

new.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 extended the franchise to about what share of the population?
new.x: The franchise rose from about 3% to about 14% of the population (about 3.5 crore voters).

new.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 extended communal representation to:
o: Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans
new.x: The 1935 Act extended communal representation to depressed classes, women and labour; the 1919 Act had covered Sikhs, Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Defence and Foreign Affairs were placed under the federal legislature.
It provided bicameral legislatures in six provinces.
It vested residuary powers in the Governor-General.
new.x: Defence and Foreign Affairs were reserved subjects under the Governor-General, not the federal legislature.

new.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, the Council of India was:
o: Merged with the Board of Control
new.x: The 1935 Act abolished the Council of India and gave the Secretary of State advisers instead.

new.s: Provincial dyarchy, introduced in 1919, was ended by the:
new.x: The 1935 Act abolished provincial dyarchy and brought provincial autonomy; dyarchy at the Centre never took effect.

new.s: The Governor-General was also styled 'Viceroy' by the:
new.x: The 1858 Act made the Governor-General also the Viceroy, Lord Canning being the first.

new.s: The Swaraj Party made the first formal demand for a Constituent Assembly in May 1934 at:
new.x: The Swaraj Party's first formal demand came at Ranchi in May 1934; the Congress adopted it at Patna.

new.s: Nehru made a clear statement of support for a Constituent Assembly in:
new.x: Nehru's clear statement came in 1938; the August Offer accepted the principle in 1940.

new.s: The Cabinet Mission arrived in India on:
new.x: The Cabinet Mission of Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps and Alexander arrived on 24 March 1946.

new.s: How many seats were allotted to the Princely States in the Constituent Assembly?
new.x: Of the 389 planned seats, 296 were for British India and 93 for the Princely States.

new.s: The provincial members of the Constituent Assembly were elected by:
o: Proportional representation by single transferable vote
new.x: Provincial Assembly members elected them by proportional representation through the single transferable vote.

new.s: Representatives of princely states first took their seats from the third session, on:
new.x: States such as Baroda, Bikaner, Jaipur, Patiala, Rewa and Udaipur joined from the third session on 28 April 1947.

new.s: Dr Sachchidananda Sinha was made temporary President as the eldest member, following the practice of:
new.x: Sinha became temporary President as the eldest member, following French practice.

new.s: The Steering Committee of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by:
new.x: Prasad chaired the Steering Committee; 'Steering Committee – Nehru' was the wrong pair in APPSC Group 1, 2004.

new.s: The States Committee, for negotiating with the princely states, was chaired by:
new.x: Nehru chaired the States Committee, as well as the Union Constitution and Union Powers Committees.

new.s: The Order of Business Committee of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by:
new.x: K.M. Munshi chaired the Order of Business Committee; Pattabhi Sitaramayya chaired the House Committee.

new.s: The 'P' in the JVP Committee stood for:
new.x: JVP stood for Jawaharlal, Vallabhbhai (Patel) and Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

new.s: Nehru accepted the demand for an Andhra province on:
new.x: Nehru accepted the Andhra demand on 27 November 1947, but Andhra was dropped from the Draft of 21 February 1948.

new.s: How many members attended the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly on 9 December 1946?
new.x: 207 members, including nine women, attended; the Muslim League boycotted the meeting.

new.s: The National Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
new.x: The National Flag was adopted on 22 July 1947; 22 January 1947 was the adoption of the Objectives Resolution.

new.s: Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected the first President of India at the Assembly's meeting on:
new.x: At the final meeting on 24 January 1950 Prasad was elected first President; on 11 December 1946 he had been elected President of the Assembly.

new.s: How many amendments to the Draft Constitution were proposed in the Constituent Assembly?
new.x: 7,635 amendments were proposed, of which 2,473 were discussed.

new.s: For how many days was the Draft Constitution considered by the Assembly?
new.x: The Draft was considered for 114 days; the Drafting Committee sat 141 days and the Assembly 165 days in all.

new.s: Vande Mataram, declared the national song, was originally composed in:
new.x: Bankimchandra's Vande Mataram was in Sanskrit, written in Bengali script.

new.s: Article 51A(a) names which national symbols for citizens to respect?
o: The National Anthem and the National Song
The National Song and the National Flag
The National Flag and the National Anthem
The National Flag, Anthem and Song
new.x: Article 51A(a) names the Flag and the Anthem, not the National Song.

new.s: The Interim Government of 1946 took charge on:
new.x: It was announced on 24 August 1946 and took charge on 2 September 1946.

new.s: Who held the Law portfolio in the Interim Government of 1946?
new.x: Jogendra Nath Mandal (League) held Law; Ambedkar later became the first Law Minister of independent India.

new.s: In the Interim Government of 1946, the Defence portfolio was held by:
new.x: Baldev Singh held Defence; Patel held Home, Jagjivan Ram Labour and Rajagopalachari Education.

new.s: The Indian Independence Bill received royal assent on:
new.x: The Bill was introduced in the Commons on 4 July 1947 and received royal assent on 18 July 1947.

new.s: The Indian Independence Bill was introduced in the House of Commons on:
new.x: It was introduced on 4 July 1947; royal assent followed on 18 July 1947.

new.s: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 was based on the:
new.x: The 3 June 1947 Plan of Mountbatten, accepted by the Congress and the League, was the basis of the Act.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mountbatten Plan:
1. It was announced on 3 June 1947.
2. It was accepted by both the Congress and the Muslim League.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: the 3 June 1947 Plan was accepted by the Congress and the League and became the basis of the Act.

new.s: The Punjab and Bengal Boundary Commissions were chaired by:
new.x: Radcliffe chaired both Boundary Commissions; the award was published on 17 August 1947.

new.s: The Radcliffe award was published on:
new.x: The award came out on 17 August 1947, two days after independence.

new.s: Hyderabad signed a Standstill Agreement with India in:
new.x: Hyderabad signed a Standstill Agreement in November 1947; Kashmir acceded on 26 October 1947.

new.s: India's dominion status came to an end on:
new.x: Dominion status ended when India became a Republic on 26 January 1950.

new.s: Who was the last and only Indian Governor-General of India?
new.x: Rajagopalachari was the last and only Indian Governor-General (June 1948-January 1950); Mountbatten was the first GG of independent India.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Independence Act, 1947:
1. The British Crown lost its veto.
2. The Central Legislative Assembly continued alongside the Constituent Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Crown lost its veto, but the Central Legislative Assembly ended; the Constituent Assembly became the Dominion legislature.

new.s: Critics said the Assembly took about 3 years, compared with about how long for the USA?
new.x: Critics called the Assembly time-consuming: about 3 years against about 4 months for the USA.

new.s: Ambedkar's phrase on constitutional morality was borrowed from:
new.x: Ambedkar's 4 November 1948 remark that constitutional morality has to be cultivated was borrowed from George Grote.

new.s: Which country has the world's first written Constitution, also the shortest with only 7 Articles?
new.x: The USA has the first and shortest written Constitution (7 Articles); Britain has no single written constitution.

new.s: Critics who called the Indian Constitution a 'lawyers' paradise' pointed to its:
new.x: 'Lawyers' paradise' refers to its legal detail; 'elephantine' refers to its length and 'bag of borrowings' to its sources.

new.s: Who called the Directive Principles a 'novel feature' of the Indian Constitution?
new.x: Ambedkar called the DPSP a 'novel feature', replying that borrowed features were adapted to Indian conditions.

new.s: The demand for a written Constitution made by Indians was accepted in principle by the:
new.x: The 1935 Act did not provide for a Constitution made by Indians; the August Offer of 1940 accepted it in principle.

new.s: Which of the following features was NOT taken from the Government of India Act, 1935?
new.x: Fundamental Duties came from the USSR; the Governor, PSCs and Emergency scheme came from the 1935 Act.

new.s: Bicameralism in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
new.x: Bicameralism, like the cabinet system and single citizenship, came from Britain (APPSC GS 2024).

new.s: Prerogative writs in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from:
new.x: Prerogative writs, parliamentary privileges and the Rule of Law came from Britain.

new.s: The office of the Speaker and his role was borrowed from:
new.x: The office of Speaker is a British parliamentary feature.

new.s: The post of Vice-President in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
new.x: The Vice-President's post came from the USA, along with impeachment and removal of judges.

new.s: The impeachment of the President was borrowed from the Constitution of:
new.x: Impeachment of the President is a US feature.

new.s: Judicial review in India is narrower than in the USA because Article 21 uses the phrase:
new.x: Article 21 uses 'procedure established by law' (from Japan), not the US 'due process'.

new.s: 'Union of States' with a strong Centre (Article 1) follows the pattern of:
new.x: India's federation with a strong Centre, a 'Union of States', follows the Canadian model.

new.s: The appointment of State Governors by the Centre was borrowed from:
new.x: Appointment of Governors by the Centre came from Canada.

new.s: If a Union law and a State law clash on a Concurrent List subject:
new.x: Both Parliament and State Legislatures legislate on the Concurrent List, but the Union law prevails in a clash.

new.s: The procedure for amendment of the Constitution (Article 368) was borrowed from:
new.x: The amendment procedure came from South Africa, not Ireland or France.

new.s: Nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha was borrowed from:
new.x: Nomination to the Rajya Sabha came from Ireland; the election of its members came from South Africa.

new.s: The phrase 'procedure established by law' in Article 21 was borrowed from:
new.x: 'Procedure established by law' came from Japan; 'due process' is the US idea.

new.s: Which Article is the most easily suspended during a National Emergency?
new.x: Article 19 is the most easily suspended; Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended.

new.s: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the:
new.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Fundamental Duties; the 86th added the eleventh duty.

new.s: The ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity in the Preamble were borrowed from:
new.x: France gave the Republic and liberty, equality and fraternity; the USSR gave the ideals of justice.

new.s: The idea of Five-Year Plans was borrowed from:
new.x: Five-Year Plans and the Planning Commission idea came from the USSR.

new.s: The Election Commission under Article 324 is:
new.x: The Election Commission is an Indian innovation, not inspired by any foreign constitution.

new.s: Originally, the State List of the Seventh Schedule contained how many subjects?
new.x: The lists were originally 97, 66 and 47; now they are 98, 59 and 52.

new.s: The joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament is provided under Article:
new.x: Article 108 provides for the joint sitting, borrowed from Australia; Article 143 is advisory jurisdiction.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Suspension of Fundamental Rights in Emergency – Weimar Germany
Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court – Australia
Freedom of trade and commerce – Canada
new.x: Suspension of FRs is from Weimar Germany; advisory jurisdiction is from Canada, freedom of trade from Australia and procedure established by law from Japan.

new.s: The independence of the judiciary was borrowed from:
new.x: Independence of the judiciary, like judicial review, came from the USA.

new.s: Which of the following designation – first holder pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India (1833); Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal and Canning the first Viceroy.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Indian Councils Act, 1861?
o: It gave statutory recognition to the portfolio system.
It gave the Viceroy an ordinance power of up to six months.
It restored the legislative powers of Bombay and Madras.
It began indirect election to the councils.
new.x: Indirect election began only with the Indian Councils Act, 1892.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the princely states in 1947?
o: Finance was ceded under the Instrument of Accession.
Defence was ceded under the Instrument of Accession.
Communications were ceded under the Instrument of Accession.
Hyderabad signed a Standstill Agreement in November 1947.
new.x: The Instrument of Accession ceded defence, external affairs and communications, not finance.

new.s: Which of the following remarks is correctly matched with its speaker?
o: Delay adult franchise by 15 years – Rajendra Prasad
'A Constitution, like a machine, is a lifeless thing' – Rajendra Prasad
new.x: Prasad said this on 26 November 1949; 'Drifting Committee' was Naziruddin Ahmed's, 'a body of Hindus' Viscount Simon's, and Maulana Azad wanted adult franchise delayed.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about federal features borrowed by the Constitution:
1. Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse was borrowed from Australia.
2. The Concurrent List was borrowed from Canada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse and the Concurrent List both came from Australia, not Canada.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT borrowed from Britain?
new.x: Judicial review came from the USA; single citizenship, Rule of Law and the cabinet system came from Britain.
